title: api-schema-versioning-deprecations-beta-headers-backcompat-shims
author: Maya Nguyen
description: Background: We are rolling out a formal API schema versioning strategy to reduce regressions across streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output while preserving OpenAI-compatibility. This PR adds header-based opt-ins for beta schema features, server-side backward-compatibility shims, and deprecation notices for legacy fields. Motivation: recent incidents (see ENG-4821) revealed multiple subtle incompatibilities between historical OpenAI-compatible shapes and the newer structured-output/function-calling objects returned by the runtime during streaming. Goal: Allow clients to opt into the new schema via a header, provide shims so old clients keep working, and centralize request/response schema mapping in the API gateway/OpenAI-compat layer so downstream SDKs can be simplified.
commits: 1) Add schema header parsing and gate logic to API gateway (two commits)
tests_added: unit tests for header parsing, shim transforms for function call shapes, streaming chunk backward compat tests and an integration matrix validating both OpenAI-compat and native schema paths
review_conversation: Carlos Rivera (2025-01-20): Nice clean split of concerns. One high-level ask: can we centralize the transformation rules so both openai-compat and runtime share the same canonical mapping?
Maya Nguyen (2025-01-20): I pulled the mapping into openai-compat/src/mapper.rs and added a thin view in runtime to reuse the logic via the crate boundary. See new module and tests.

Anika Patel (2025-01-22): We need to be explicit about stream chunk typing changes. I'm seeing a potential client break where older clients expect a final 'done' event with 'choices[*].message' and newer schema emits 'delta' events only. Please add a compatibility chunk that emits 'done' for legacy-specified clients.

Maya Nguyen (2025-01-23): Added streaming_shims.rs to map new delta-only streams to legacy 'done' finalizers when the client does not opt into the new schema. Also added an opt-in header Redwood-API-Schema: v2 (beta) and Redwood-Beta: streaming_schema. The gateway honors these headers and will forward schema=v2 to the runtime.

Lars Möller (2025-01-27): CI matrix failing in one job (py sdk OpenAI-compat mappings). Root cause: the previous mapping left 'function_call.arguments' as a JSON-string in the compatibility path. We should deserialize it for the shim.
Maya Nguyen (2025-01-28): Fixed deserialization edge-case and added unit + e2e tests. Reran the matrix.
Carlos Rivera (2025-02-03): Approval after tests stable and docs reviewed. Left a minor nit about wording in migration docs.
Anika Patel (2025-02-04): Approved. Recommend release notes entry.
ci_summary: Initial CI: failed (integration matrix job 'py-sdk/openai-compat' failed). After fix and rebase CI: pass. Full matrix green including eslint, unit tests, e2e streaming tests, and schema-versioning matrix build.
migration_guide: docs/migrations/schema_migration_guide.md includes header usage, examples for Typescript and Python SDKs, and recommended rollout steps: 1) start servers with 'fallback: true' for 2 weeks, 2) add Redwood-API-Schema: v2 to client to opt-in, 3) monitor schema_version metric and error rates, 4) disable fallback once adoption >= 95%.
release_notes:
* Introduces API schema versioning (header-based opt-in via Redwood-API-Schema)
* Adds backward-compatibility shims for streaming deltas and function-calling shapes
* Updates OpenAI-compat layer to map v2 structured output to legacy OpenAI response shapes
* Docs and migration guide included
followups: ENG-4987: Automate deprecation emails and SDK warnings; ENG-4999: Add telemetry to measure full client adoption for schema v2
notes: The header name and values are intentionally conservative: Redwood-API-Schema: v2 and Redwood-Beta: streaming_schema. We avoid changing the default behavior (clients without headers see legacy shapes). This PR intentionally does not flip default schema to avoid global client regressions. SDK updates include helper wrappers that set headers by default once the SDK major version is bumped.
